risks.title: Raw marker hiding needs an editable token layer
risks.summary: Raw and split source highlighting are implemented with a synchronized Highlight.js overlay, but hiding markdown markers still requires a true editable token/decoration layer.
mitigations: Keep Hide markers off the screen
Use the shared highlighter overlay for visible source syntax tinting
Add a future task to vendor a markdown-capable editable decoration layer before implementing marker hiding

risks.title: Future concept controls can be mistaken for finished features
risks.summary: The concept includes Preview, Share, Export, image, math, help, marker controls, and scroll locking that are not all backed by current subsystems.
mitigations: Remove unsupported enabled controls from the current screen
Enforce no-decorative-control behavior in e2e tests
Track deferred subsystems in planning docs and release truth

risks.title: WYSIWYG editing rewrites markdown it cannot represent
risks.summary:
The WYSIWYG surface parses markdown into the vendored ProseMirror model and re-serializes the WHOLE document, so any construct the model cannot express is rewritten or lost, and because an edit replaces the entire buffer the blast radius of one keystroke is the whole file. Measured: inline
deleted (joining adjacent words), link reference definitions deleted and inlined, CRLF rewritten whole-file, plus respellings of bullets, fences, setext headings, hard breaks and thematic breaks. Accepted for the 0.4.0 GA by maintainer decision with disclosure as the mitigation; the defect itself is open.
mitigations: README leads with a caution naming each rewrite and directing users to Raw mode when exact bytes matter
e2e/fidelity_test.go measures the behaviour so the caution cannot drift from the code
Raw mode preserves every affected construct and is the documented safe path
Evaluate a replacement editing engine: a CommonMark-faithful schema, or source-preserving editing where WYSIWYG edits patch the original text instead of replacing it with a re-serialization

risks.title: Saving clobbers changes made outside the app
risks.summary: Nothing compares modification time, size or content before overwriting. A file changed on disk since it was opened — by a git pull, a sync client, or a second window — is replaced silently with no error. Raised as a blocking finding in ABORT Round 1 and carried across three rounds without a recorded justification.
mitigations: Disclosed in the README's Known limitations
Record the content or modification time at open and refuse or prompt when it has changed at save

risks.title: Replacement by rename loses file identity and metadata
risks.summary: Saving writes a temp file and renames it over the target. That breaks hard links to the document, drops extended attributes such as Finder tags, and replaces a read-only file, because rename needs permission on the directory rather than on the file.
mitigations: Disclosed in the README's Known limitations
Copy extended attributes onto the temp file before rename, and refuse a target the user cannot write

risks.title: Asset containment bounds the directory but not the file type
risks.summary: A document may only reference assets at or below its own directory, which is enforced. But a non-image extension falls back to application/octet-stream and its bytes are still inlined, so any file at or below the document directory is readable on render — and rendering is automatic, with no user interaction. For a markdown file opened from a Downloads folder or a repository root, that set is not small.
mitigations: Restrict inlining to the known image extensions and refuse everything else
Refusals already surface through the existing missing-asset render state

risks.title: No logging, crash record or error trail reaches the maintainer
risks.summary: Frontend diagnostics are console warnings with no devtools in a production build; Go errors surface only as an ephemeral modal carrying the error string. Nothing is persisted. A bug reported by a user cannot be tied to a build or reproduced from recorded state, which this project's own rules require of any new failure surface.
mitigations: Version identity now ships in the bundle so a report can at least name the build
Add a structured event trail persisted beside the preference store

risks.title: Every release gate is hand-run and nothing enforces them
risks.summary: There is no CI configuration in the repository. Tests, vet, Architext validation, screenshot regeneration, vendoring and packaging are all run by hand, so forgetting any one of them is silent — and the release artifact was in fact found two rounds stale during ABORT Round 4.
mitigations: Disclosed in the ABORT artifact
Add a workflow running go test, go vet and architext validate on push

risks.title: Vendored editor bundles carry no integrity record
risks.summary: tools/vendor.sh fetches several megabytes of third-party JavaScript over the network and records no checksum; NOTICE.md records package and version but no hash, and the committed bundle is patched in place so it matches no upstream artifact. Provenance cannot be re-established later.
mitigations: Record a SHA-256 per bundle in NOTICE.md and verify it in vendor.sh before writing
